key_insight: Structurally consistent approximate-deconvolution LES closures improve stability, while the proposed A-LDMK most accurately predicts atomization droplet sizes among the assessed closures.
engineering_relevance: These models could improve turbulent gas–liquid atomization simulations where multiscale breakup and droplet size distributions are important.
method: Extend structurally consistent approximate-deconvolution closures to two-phase LES.
Introduce A-LDMK, a non-equilibrium mixed eddy-viscosity model with a kinetic-energy equation.
Evaluate closures a posteriori in channel flow and a gas–liquid mixing layer.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved numerical stability and sustained energy backscatter under less restrictive stability constraints, with A-LDMK giving the best droplet size distribution prediction among tested closures.
watch_item: Validation is limited to the reported test cases; broader applicability and quantitative accuracy gains are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Novel Mixed Approximate Deconvolution Large-Eddy Simulation Models for Two-Phase Flows
